images.filename: A view of a 179-ton steel Tainter gate (15953809716).jpg
images.caption: A view of aTainter gate for the Folsom Dam auxiliary spillway in Folsom, Calif., Dec. 05, 2014. The 179-ton steel gate is one of six Tainter gates that will control water flow from Folsom Lake into the new auxiliary spillway. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District, together with the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation and state and local partners, is building the spillway to reduce flood risk throughout the Sacramento region. (U.S. Army photo by SFC Jeremy M. Nelson/Released)
images.alt: A view of aTainter gate for the Folsom Dam auxiliary spillway in Folsom, Calif., Dec. 05, 2014. images.caption:
FOLSOM, Calif. (May 4, 2011) – Project managers Pamela Amie from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District and Mark Curney from the Bureau of Reclamation explain the phases of the Joint Federal Project (JFP) to participants of the Water Education Foundation’s Flood Management tour at the Folsom Dam and auxiliary spillway here May 4.

Amie, one of three Corps project managers for the JFP, joined Corps water manager Kyle Keer at the two-day event, which runs through May 5 and aims to educate participants on the Corps role in flood risk reduction. The tour – attended by many water experts and engineering consultants from throughout California – will include field trips to the Bear River, West Sacramento, the Pocket area and several of the area’s weirs.

images.caption: FOLSOM, Calif. – Construction of the Folsom Dam auxiliary spillway continues here Jan. 20, part of the Folsom Dam Joint Federal Project between the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, the Sacramento Area Flood Control Agency and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District to reduce flood risk for the Sacramento area. The spillway will allow for slower and safer water releases from Folsom Lake into the American River in high water. The Sacramento District completed the Folsom Lake Crossing Bridge across the river (shown at bottom) in 2009, replacing the road atop the dam closed for security concerns in 2003.
images.alt: FOLSOM, Calif. – Construction of the Folsom Dam auxiliary spillway continues here Jan. 20, part of the Folsom Dam Joint Federal Project between the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, the Sacramento Area Flood Control Agency and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District to reduce flood risk for the Sacramento area. The spillway will allow for slower and safer water releases from Folsom Lake into the American River in high water. The Sacramento District completed the Folsom Lake Crossing Bridge across the river (shown at bottom) in 2009, replacing the road atop the dam closed for security concerns in 2003.
